references.text: Abraham also asks God not to become angry as he continues to pray, using similar respectful language when addressing God repeatedly.
Moses asks the Lord not to let his anger burn against the people, a similar prayer that God's wrath should not flare up.
The preceding account where Gideon first asks for the sign with the fleece and dew, which this prayer continues.
Gideon previously asked for a sign from God to confirm his calling, showing a pattern of seeking divine confirmation.
The Lord offers King Ahaz a sign, demonstrating that God sometimes gives signs to confirm His word.
Jesus refers to an evil and unfaithful generation that seeks signs, providing perspective on asking God for signs.
